subject.title: Widget cost rows wrap awkwardly with large token counts

question: Which medium-widget behavior should be the supported narrow-width contract for large token estimates: abbreviated single-line values, a fixed/adaptive value column, or a deliberate vertical fallback?
rationale: The report identifies the visual failure but presents several valid UX directions; selecting one affects widget readability, localization headroom, and future formatting consistency.

options.title: Abbreviate and preserve one line
options.body: Format large token totals with compact units and give the primary cost/value line priority within the existing two-column row.

options.title: Adopt an adaptive grid
options.body: Keep detailed token values when width permits, but use explicit column priorities or a vertical fallback at constrained widths.

options.title: Keep current formatting
options.body: Decline the layout change and document the existing wrapping as an accepted compact-widget trade-off.

recommendation.title: Abbreviate and preserve one line
recommendation.body: Format large token totals with compact units and give the primary cost/value line priority within the existing two-column row.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership is the only available routing signal while local history inspection is unavailable.
